definition: In linguistics and natural language processing, a corpus (pl.: corpora) or text corpus is a dataset, consisting of natively digital and older, digitalized, language resources, either annotated or unannotated.
details: Annotated, they have been used in corpus linguistics for statistical hypothesis testing, checking occurrences or validating linguistic rules within a specific language territory.
story: Imagine a chef tasting every ingredient before it goes into the pot, deciding what belongs and what would ruin the broth. Better ingredients make a better meal, and the same is true here. Every machine is shaped by what it was shown, so someone has to choose that material with care. It is the raw material; the model is only ever as good as what it was fed. And that is Text corpus — the unglamorous work everything else stands on.
